source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026)
finding: Frames case reuse as a contextual bandit. Each candidate case is an arm; context is query plus case; reward is binary task success of the LLM answer. Only the retriever (a reranker plus linear head) learns; the LLM is frozen. Only successful cases are retained.
numbers: Case = (query, answer, reward). Two-stage retrieval: fixed embedder recalls K=32 candidates, trained reranker picks one. Pick rule is UCB: linear-head score plus alpha times uncertainty of the encoder feature (Eq 7). Linear head updated by one gradient step per step; encoder updated every H steps by batch logistic loss.
limits: Preprint (arXiv v1, 5 May 2026), no peer review seen. Single case per prompt in main results. Reward is binary and assumed stationary.
agent_relevance: Our class record could be the arm set; reward = did this case help the next problem pass a held-out check.

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) regret decomposition
finding: Splits regret into a coverage gap (no good case exists in the bank) and retrieval regret (a good case exists but the retriever picked a worse one). The bank growing closes the first; the bandit closes the second.
numbers: Eq 4. Theorem 1: coverage gap is O~(T^((d0-1)/d0)) for intrinsic dimension d0>1, O~(1) if d0<=1. Theorem 2: retrieval regret O~(B*sqrt(T)/kappa), kappa = sigmoid monotonicity constant, B = reward-model approximation error. Total is sublinear (Theorem 3).
limits: Needs 3 assumptions: similar queries have similar best cases (Lipschitz), the frozen LLM keeps a positive chance of success given a correct case, queries are i.i.d. Real task streams break i.i.d. Bounds are informal in main text; neural-width conditions are asymptotic.
agent_relevance: Gives a clean test: measure how often the best stored case exists (coverage) separately from how often we pick it (retrieval).

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) main results Qwen3-32B
finding: Over 12 single-turn tasks, learned retrieval beats non-learned case retrieval (NP-CBR) by 2.92 points on average, and beats zero-shot by 18.35 points.
numbers: Table S5/S4, Qwen3-32B, 5 seeds: zero-shot 48.33; ICRL 52.48; ICRLPlus 54.33; REINFORCE+LoRA 58.93; NP-CBR 63.76; CASCADE 66.68 (average success %). CASCADE beats REINFORCE+LoRA on 9 of 12 tasks; with 4 cases it beats it on the other 3.
limits: Most of the gain over zero-shot comes from having cases at all (NP-CBR is +15.4 of the +18.35). The bandit part is the final +2.92. Zero-shot average is printed as 48.33 for both 14B and 32B, which looks like a table duplicate. The abstract says +20.9% macro over 16 tasks; we cannot reproduce 20.9 from 66.68 vs 48.33 (18.35 points absolute, 38% relative), so the metric is unresolved.
agent_relevance: Honest size of the 'learned value' effect: about 3 points on top of plain similarity retrieval.

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) ablation Table S5
finding: Removing exploration costs little; swapping in a weaker bandit costs more. The exploration bonus is the smallest contributor.
numbers: Qwen3-32B averages: full 66.68; w/o exploration (alpha=0) 66.37 (-0.31); NeuralLinUCB 65.49; NeuralLogUCB 65.39; LinLogUCB 63.95; no bandit (NP-CBR) 63.76. Task-level: SEntFiN 48.37 w/o exploration vs 47.72 full; MIMIC-IV-TLP 57.09 vs 56.79; NeuralLogUCB beats full on MIMIC-IV-MSR (53.00 vs 52.25) and BIRD (56.21 vs 55.18).
limits: Five seeds, per-task standard deviations 0.1 to 1.0, so the 0.31 gap is inside noise on several tasks. Linear bandit on frozen features gains only +0.19 over no bandit. No significance test reported.
agent_relevance: Most gain comes from LEARNING a value from outcomes, not from clever exploration. Cheap greedy-by-outcome may capture most of it.

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) exploration coefficient and scale
finding: Gain over NP-CBR is positive across alpha 0.1 to 1.0 in most settings, but best alpha differs by task. Backbone must be able to succeed at least sometimes.
numbers: Qwen3-8B avg 60.84 vs NP-CBR 58.44 (+2.40); 14B 65.10 vs 62.81 (+2.29); 32B 66.68 vs 63.76 (+2.92). Authors suggest alpha=0.1 default. Qwen3-4B: all methods fail on MIMIC-IV-MR. CASCADE lower bound beats zero-shot upper bound in 9 of 12 tasks.
limits: Learning needs nonzero base success: 'when zero-shot is near zero, learning from experience becomes substantially more challenging'. Per-task tuning was used for the baseline bandits in the ablation.
agent_relevance: Bandit/value learning will do nothing on problems the model never solves; do not expect it to rescue those.

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) multi-turn and deep search
finding: Trajectory-level cases with learned retrieval beat plain similarity retrieval in embodied and tool-use tasks; gains are larger on harder tasks.
numbers: ALFWorld 62.01 -> 67.43 (NP-CBR -> CASCADE), zero-shot 39.69 (Act). ScienceWorld 59.36 -> 66.84, zero-shot 30.71. With ReAct: ALFWorld 80.76 -> 81.74; ScienceWorld 71.52 -> 74.67; zero-shot ReAct 62.35 / 55.55. 2Wiki (Qwen3-30B-A3B): local RAG 45.94 -> 50.06 (no tools 20.29, zero-shot with tool 35.36); web search 53.29 -> 66.51 (zero-shot 50.63). MIMIC-III EHR: zero-shot 20.75, NP-CBR 44.02, CASCADE 55.76. 134 unseen ALFWorld tasks: about 2x zero-shot.
limits: Five seeds. With ReAct the bandit gain shrinks to +0.98 and +3.15 points. EHR NP-CBR cited as prior state of the art. Task distribution i.i.d. in-stream.
agent_relevance: Evidence that retrieval choice matters most when a task has long traces and many near-duplicate but unequally useful cases.

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) human discovery steps (E-E-D)
finding: Using the bandit's own score to decide when to ask for a human label helps more than asking at random.
numbers: 10% discovery budget; trigger when metric below the 10th percentile of a FIFO queue of 16. Average relative gain over standard CASCADE: Exploit metric +8.83%, UCB +8.73%, random +5.61%.
limits: Simulation with ground-truth labels, 12 single-turn tasks, Qwen3-32B.
agent_relevance: A value score doubles as a 'no good case here' detector, which maps to our impasse signal (G1).

source: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment (Guo, Du, Chen, Chang, Wang 2026) limitations
finding: Authors list: long-horizon memory growth and forgetting untested; failed attempts are discarded; needs minimal base competence.
numbers: Retain rule: keep case only if r=1. Baselines DC and ACE were dropped because they degrade on weaker backbones.
limits: Self-reported limits; no independent replication seen.
agent_relevance: Matches our own open question on whether storing only successes loses useful traps (see retention subfield).

source: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs (Zhou et al. 2025)
finding: Treats case selection as a memory-augmented MDP and learns a case-level Q-function by soft Q-learning, so retrieval becomes a softmax over learned values. Stores both successes and failures.
numbers: Policy pi(c|s,M) proportional to exp(Q(s,M,c)/tau). Parametric version: SimCSE encoder plus Q head, top-K by Q. GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%; DeepResearcher 66.6 F1 / 80.4 PM; OOD gain from case bank +4.7 to +9.6 points.
limits: Planner GPT-4.1 and executor o3/o4-mini. Authors note possible contamination in DeepResearcher benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Earliest LLM-agent case of Q-learned retrieval; value learning on cases is cheap.

source: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs (Zhou et al. 2025) learned vs similarity retrieval
finding: Learned (parametric) case retrieval beats similarity retrieval, but only by under 1.1 points per iteration, and the benefit of any case memory shrinks with more iterations.
numbers: DeepResearcher accuracy over 5 iterations. No CBR: 78.65, 80.93, 82.62, 83.53, 84.47. Non-parametric CBR: 79.84, 81.87, 83.09, 84.03, 84.85. Parametric CBR: 80.46, 82.84, 84.10, 84.85, 85.44. Parametric minus non-parametric: +0.62, +0.97, +1.01, +0.82, +0.59.
limits: No seeds or confidence intervals reported. Authors say the bank saturates quickly with about 3k training items and they could not find any performance drop along the curve.
agent_relevance: Learned value over similarity is a small, hard-to-see gain on a task where similarity retrieval already works.

source: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs (Zhou et al. 2025) number of retrieved cases
finding: Adding cases helps up to a few, then flat. One case already gives most of the gain.
limits: Same benchmark as above. Table 5 shows tool use alone hurt DeepResearcher by 18.0 F1.
agent_relevance: Supports using few (1-4) selected cases, not a long list.

source: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime RL on Episodic Memory (Zhang et al. 2026)
finding: Each memory item stores intent, experience and a learned utility Q. Retrieval is two-phase: recall by cosine similarity (threshold, top-k1), then rank by a blend of z-scored similarity and z-scored Q. Q is updated by a Monte Carlo rule from task reward.
numbers: score = (1-lambda)*z(similarity) + lambda*z(Q). Best lambda = 0.5 (inverted-U over 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1). Pure similarity plateaus; lambda near 1 is volatile.
limits: Preprint (v2, 12 Feb 2026). Not a bandit with explicit exploration bonus; exploration comes from similarity term and the frozen LLM.
agent_relevance: A simple, ready-made recipe for our class record: blend similarity with a running success value.

source: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime RL on Episodic Memory (Zhang et al. 2026) runtime and transfer results
finding: Utility-ranked memory beats RAG, Self-RAG, Mem0 and MemP across four benchmarks.
numbers: Runtime (last epoch / cumulative), average across benchmarks: no memory 0.631; RAG 0.679/0.699; Mem0 0.681/0.712; MemP 0.736/0.760; MemRL 0.772/0.798. Per task last-epoch: BigCodeBench 0.595 (MemP 0.578), OS 0.788 (0.736), DB 0.960 (0.960), ALFWorld 0.949 (0.885), HLE 0.570 (0.522). Transfer to held-out sets (frozen bank): MemRL 0.794 vs MemP 0.766 vs no memory 0.709. Different backbones per benchmark (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5-mini, Gemini-3-pro).
limits: The runtime table scores repeated epochs over the same task set, so last-epoch success partly reflects having seen the tasks. DB task is a tie. No seeds or error bars in the tables I read.
agent_relevance: Held-out transfer is the number to trust: +2.8 points over the best rival, +8.5 over no memory.

source: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime RL on Episodic Memory (Zhang et al. 2026) Q-value validity and failure memories
finding: Learned Q correlates with real success, and about 12% of high-Q memories are failures kept as useful near-misses.
numbers: Pearson r = 0.861 between Q and empirical success; success rises from 21.5% in the lowest Q bin to 88.1% in the highest. Forgetting rate 0.041 for MemRL, MemP 0.051.
limits: Correlation measured on the agent's own training stream, not a fresh test.
agent_relevance: Q is a usable predicted-help score; check it against held-out outcomes before trusting it.

source: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime RL on Episodic Memory (Zhang et al. 2026) boundary conditions
finding: Value learning helps only when tasks recur and look alike; where tasks are semantically scattered it reduces to single-task reflection.
numbers: Cross-task MemRL vs single-task reflection (Reflexion-like): average 0.798 vs 0.761; OS +9.0, ALFWorld +5.1 points; on HLE they tie (0.606 vs 0.610) because internal task similarity is 0.186. Retrieval size on HLE subset: k1=5,k2=3 best; sparse (3/1) and dense (10/5) worse.
limits: Authors admit step-wise update has high variance in long traces and credit assignment is unclear when several memories are shown together.
agent_relevance: Shows when NOT to expect gains: low-similarity problem streams like our mixed puzzle classes.

source: Li, Chu, Langford, Schapire (2010) A contextual-bandit approach to personalized news article recommendation (LinUCB)
finding: Founding contextual-bandit method used by the CBR-bandit line: pick the arm with highest linear score plus a confidence-width bonus; also gives an unbiased offline replay evaluation for bandits from random logs.
numbers: Yahoo Front Page Today Module, over 33 million events. LinUCB hybrid gave up to 12.5% click lift over context-free epsilon-greedy; lift around 10% for feature-using methods in general; larger when data is scarce (small learning bucket). Omniscient context-free CTR was 1.615 (normalised to random).
limits: Feature-using methods needed good features; epsilon-greedy and UCB with warm start were less stable in deployment. Click reward is single-step with no delayed effect.
agent_relevance: LinUCB-style scoring is the linear ancestor of CASCADE's Neural-LinLogUCB; the offline replay method lets us test a retrieval policy from logs.

source: Zhou, Li, Gu (2020) Neural contextual bandits with UCB-based exploration (NeuralUCB)
finding: First neural contextual bandit with a near-optimal regret bound; uses neural-tangent features for the confidence bonus.
numbers: Regret O~(sqrt(T)) in effective-dimension terms, with only a boundedness assumption on reward; tested on UCI sets (covertype, magic, statlog) and MNIST in the paper.
limits: Guarantee needs very wide networks; I read abstract, intro and theorem statements only.
agent_relevance: CASCADE compares to this family (NeuralLogUCB, NeuralLinUCB); the ablation shows the family differs by 1 to 2 points.

source: Zhang, Zhou, Li, Gu (2021) Neural Thompson Sampling
finding: Thompson-sampling twin of NeuralUCB with the same sqrt(T) regret.
numbers: Cumulative regret O(T^(1/2)) given bounded reward.
limits: I read abstract and opening only. Not used by CASCADE or MemRL.
agent_relevance: A sampling-based option (no extra bonus constant) if tuning alpha is a nuisance.

source: Riquelme, Tucker, Snoek (2018) Deep Bayesian bandits showdown
finding: Compared many ways to get uncertainty for Thompson sampling on contextual bandits; no method won everywhere, but a Bayesian linear regression on the last layer of a deep net was the robust, easy-to-tune choice.
numbers: Dropout, noise injection and bootstrapping helped on some tasks but failed on hard synthetic exploration; variational and MCMC methods broke when representation and uncertainty were trained together online.
quote: making decisions according to a Bayesian linear regression on the representation provided by the last layer of a deep network offers a robust and easy-to-tune approach
limits: Benchmarks are synthetic and UCI; not LLM retrieval.
agent_relevance: Direct support for CASCADE's neural-linear split (learn features, keep uncertainty linear and cheap).

source: Russo, Van Roy, Kazerouni, Osband, Wen (2018) A tutorial on Thompson sampling
finding: Standard reference for TS: practical modelling, prior choice, and what goes wrong with misspecified priors.
numbers: Shows a misspecified prior raises regret and delays learning (banner example, Fig 6.2).
limits: I only skimmed headings and the prior-misspecification section.
agent_relevance: If we use sampling-based selection, prior choice for a new class with few cases matters.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning to retrieve prompts for in-context learning (EPR)
finding: Label each stored example by how much it raises the LM's probability of the right output, then train a dense retriever on that signal. This is learned value without any exploration.
numbers: Test results vs strongest prior retriever: BREAK 26.0 -> 31.9; MTOP 57.0 -> 64.2; SMCalFlow 51.4 -> 54.3 (BM25 or CBR baselines). Random selection: 1.7 / 7.3 / 8.9.
limits: Supervised on gold outputs from a training set, static after training; no online feedback and no exploration. Three semantic-parsing datasets only.
agent_relevance: Shows value-trained retrieval beats similarity even offline; the bandit adds online adaptation.

source: Wang, Yang, Wei (2024) Learning to retrieve in-context examples for LLMs (LLM-R)
finding: Reward model from LLM log-probabilities distilled into a dense retriever, iterated; learned retriever beats BM25 and off-the-shelf dense retrievers.
numbers: 30 tasks, LLaMA-7B, 8 examples: random 57.9; K-means 57.0; BM25 61.3; E5 61.4; SBERT 62.1; EPR 63.5; LLM-R 1 iteration 65.7; 2 iterations 66.5; 3 iterations 66.4. Reported +7.8% over random on average.
limits: Offline, gold-label training; gains per task category vary (reading comprehension and sentiment barely move). Iteration 3 adds nothing.
agent_relevance: Gain of learned over BM25 about 4 to 5 points; same order as CASCADE's 3 points over reranker.

source: Zhang, Feng, Tan (2022) Active example selection for in-context learning
finding: Casts demonstration choice as a sequential decision problem and trains an offline conservative Q-learning policy. Gains are real on small models and vanish on large ones.
numbers: GPT-2: +12.1% over a max-entropy active-learning baseline on a seen task; +5.8% on average on unseen tasks. Random 4-example sets spread more than 30 points on GPT-2; after calibration AGNews still spans 79.5 max to 26.1 min. Improvement diminishes on larger GPT-3 models.
limits: Small models, short context, text classification. Authors read the vanishing gain as an emergent-capability effect.
agent_relevance: Warning: selection effects shrink as models get stronger; test on our strongest model, not a small one.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Single-episode memory of verbal self-feedback; MemRL uses it as the 'no cross-task retrieval' control.
numbers: In MemRL Table 3 the Reflexion-like single-task setting averages 0.761 vs MemRL 0.798.
limits: Only the first page was read; numbers here come from MemRL's comparison, not Reflexion itself.
agent_relevance: Separates 'learn from this task's own failures' from 'choose among past tasks'.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Retrieves the top-k stored trajectories by fixed task similarity (inner product, FAISS) and adds extracted insights; no learned value.
numbers: Method text only: retrieval by task similarity, k trajectories as few-shot examples; result tables not extracted.
limits: I read method passages, not the result tables.
agent_relevance: Baseline family that CASCADE, Memento and MemRL claim to beat: similarity-only retrieval.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank: scaling agent self-evolving with reasoning memory
finding: Embedding-similarity retrieval of distilled strategies (successes and failures); deliberately no learned retriever. Shows more retrieved items hurts.
numbers: WebArena overall success, Gemini-2.5-flash: no memory 40.5, Synapse 42.1, AWM 44.1, ReasoningBank 48.8, +MaTTS 51.8. Shopping subset by number of retrieved experiences: 0 -> 39.0; 1 -> 49.7; 2 -> 46.5; 3 -> 45.5; 4 -> 44.4.
limits: Authors kept retrieval simple on purpose to isolate content quality; success labels come from an LLM judge (about 72.7% accurate in their check).
agent_relevance: Top-1 beating top-4 is a direct argument for choosing few cases by value.

source: Thompson (1933) and Auer, Cesa-Bianchi, Fischer (2002) classic bandit work
finding: UCB1 (Auer et al. 2002) and Thompson sampling (Thompson 1933) are the two classic exploration rules behind all of the above.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers recorded.
limits: Not read this session.
agent_relevance: Background only.

source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) Case-based reasoning: foundational issues (4R cycle)
finding: Source of the Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle that CASCADE and Memento map onto a bandit loop.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Not read this session; cited through CASCADE and Memento text.
agent_relevance: Background only.
